prompt: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions and interactions, and the setting; keep the caption concrete and image‑centered and avoid speculation or subjective judgments. For every person or object state whether it is stationary or moving; when describing motion give horizontal direction first then vertical (for example, "walking from left to right," "moving toward the camera while descending"), specify the visible phase of motion when apparent (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing), indicate whether motions are simultaneous or sequential, and describe each moving subject’s trajectory relative to the main subject and relative to the camera (e.g., passing to his right, approaching from behind, moving alongside). Describe body posture using concrete camera‑relative terms (standing upright, weight shifted onto left/right leg, slight forward/back lean from the waist, seated, reclining, crouching, mid‑jump, arms outstretched, knees bent) and specify orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera). For interactions with objects or structures state exactly how the subject is using them (holding/gripping/resting on/pulling/supporting/bracing/leaning on), name which hand (left/right) and which side, and indicate whether the hand is in contact, gripping, merely near, in motion, or resting. Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow) and identify gaze targets or direction (eyes looking down at the object in her hands, gaze directed at the camera). Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts and arrangement of people or vehicles (two people side by side, a row of three boats), and proximity and scale (a few feet/meters apart, clustered closely, towering behind); use "in front of," "over," or "directly above/overhead" rather than ambiguous "above." Describe lighting, shadows, and visible surface textures with observable cues and approximate shadow direction or length (bright direct sunlight casting long shadows toward the lower left, diffuse overcast, wet pavement, reflections, motion blur). Avoid hypothetical explanations or unverifiable attributes; remain tightly grounded in visible details. Output exactly one single sentence.
